For Hebrew that produces three distinct failures:"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"1. **Whole paragraphs read backwards.** A Hebrew sentence is laid out as an LTR paragraph, so its li"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"nes start on the wrong side and punctuation lands at the wrong end. 2. **Typing into a field runs th"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"e wrong way.** The `ask_user_question` custom-answer field inherits the page direction, so Hebrew ty"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"ped into it flows left-to-right. 3. **`Cmd`+`←`/`→` feel inverted.** These shortcuts are *logical* i"},{"id":"p7s5","text":"n every browser: `←` goes to the line's logical start, which on an RTL line sits at the visual **rig"},{"id":"p7s6","text":"ht** edge. Pressing `←` jumps the caret to the far right."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"The obvious CSS answer — `unicode-bidi: plaintext` — fixes only the easy half. It picks a block's di"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"rection from its **first strong directional character**, so a Hebrew sentence that opens with a Lati"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"n product name, a list number, or an emoji is still rendered LTR and still reads garbled."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"## What this plugin does"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"### Any line with Hebrew in it is RTL"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"The rule is deliberately blunt: a block (`p`, `ul`/`ol`, `h1`–`h6`, `blockquote`, `table`) or a line"},{"id":"p11s2","text":" of text that contains **even one Hebrew letter** is forced to `direction: rtl` + `text-align: right"},{"id":"p11s3","text":"`. A block with no Hebrew is left to `unicode-bidi: plaintext`."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"Forced blocks get `unicode-bidi: isolate`, so the Unicode Bidi algorithm still lays out the Latin ru"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"ns correctly **inside** the RTL line:"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"**Why not count which script dominates.** Earlier versions counted Hebrew words against Latin words "},{"id":"p14s2","text":"and followed the majority.
